cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3). He just finished a lament for Tyre, the rich trading city by the sea (Ezekiel 27:2-3). Now God sends word to Tyre's ruler, and it starts with this: your heart is proud.

cards.question: The proud ruler of Tyre has been saying something big about himself. What is it?
God answers the ruler of Tyre's claim. True or false: God says he is a man and not a god.

cards.text: Then God says to him, “Behold, you are wiser than Daniel; no secret is hidden from you!” That's Daniel, the young exile God gave wisdom and understanding in Babylon (Daniel 1:17-20), and this ruler is the one in the group chat who already knows the news before you finish typing it.

cards.question: The ruler of Tyre has piled up gold and silver in his treasuries. How does God say he gained all that wealth?

cards.text: His great skill in trading keeps the money rolling in. Friend, I once shared a junk drawer with an expired coupon that still believed in itself, and even IT never called itself a god.

cards.question: God says the ruler of Tyre's heart has grown proud because of his ___.

cards.text: Then comes the word “Therefore,” and friend, when your boss starts a sentence with that, NOBODY is getting a raise. Because the ruler regards his heart as the heart of a god, God will bring foreigners against him.

cards.question: God is bringing foreigners against the ruler of Tyre. What kind of nations does God call them?
True or false: the foreigners will draw their swords against the beauty of the ruler of Tyre's wisdom.

cards.text: They will bring him down to the Pit, and he will die a violent death in the heart of the seas. The heart of the sea is where he said he sat. Now it's where he goes down.

cards.question: God asks if the ruler of Tyre will still call himself a god in front of those who slay him. In their hands, what will he be?
True or false: God says the ruler of Tyre will die at the hands of his own people.

cards.text: He will die the death of the uncircumcised at the hands of foreigners, and God closes with, “For I have spoken, declares the Lord GOD.” But the LORD isn't done talking about Tyre yet.
The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again. This time God tells him to take up a lament for the king of Tyre.

cards.question: True or false: the lament begins by calling the king of Tyre full of wisdom and perfect in beauty.

cards.text: Then God tells him, “You were in Eden, the garden of God.” Not the docks. Not the throne room. EDEN.

cards.question: In the lament, God describes how the king of Tyre was adorned in Eden. With what?

cards.text: Ruby, topaz, diamond and more, nine kinds of stone in all, set in gold and prepared on the day of his creation. Friend, I stand on ONE gold base and I thought I was dressed up.

cards.question: God says He had ordained the king of Tyre. What does God say he was anointed as?

cards.text: He was on the holy mountain of God, and he walked among the fiery stones. Friend, I work next to hot ovens all day, and I STILL can't walk past one without saying ow.

cards.question: True or false: God says the king of Tyre was wicked in his ways from the day he was created.

cards.text: He was blameless in his ways until wickedness was found in him, and friend, that one little word “until” just broke my heart. By the vastness of his trade, he was filled with violence, and he sinned.

cards.question: After the king of Tyre sinned, what does God say He did?

answers.text: Drove him from the mountain of God
Kept him on the mountain in chains
Sent him off to rule the seas

cards.question: God says the king of Tyre's heart grew proud of his ___.

cards.text: He corrupted his wisdom because of his splendor, so God cast him to the earth. From the holy mountain to the ground, friend, and I thought the trip from the counter to the junk drawer was a long way down.

cards.question: God casts the king of Tyre to the earth. Before whom does God make him a spectacle?

cards.text: His many iniquities and his dishonest trading profaned his sanctuaries. Trading again.

cards.question: God says He made something come from within the king of Tyre. What was it?

cards.text: God reduced him to ashes on the ground in the eyes of all who saw him. This is the one who walked among the fiery stones, and now the fire comes from inside him.

cards.question: True or false: the lament ends with the nations who know the king of Tyre celebrating his fall.

cards.text: The nations who know him are appalled, and the lament ends, “You have come to a horrible end and will be no more.” Friend, that's the kind of line where the whole bakery goes quiet.

The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel one more time. Now he's told to set his face against Sidon, a city named in the lament for Tyre too (Ezekiel 27:8), and prophesy against her. Friend, when God tells you to set your FACE at a city, that is NOT a polite email.

cards.question: God's message opens with 'Behold, I am against you, O Sidon' and keeps going. True or false: God also says He will be glorified within Sidon.
God says He will carry out judgments against Sidon. When He does, what does He say they will know?
God says trouble is coming to Sidon's own streets. What two things does He send against her?

cards.text: The slain will fall within her, with the sword against her on every side. That line again: “Then they will know that I am the LORD.”
Then the word against Sidon goes on with “For,” and it's about the people of Israel and everyone around them who treats them with contempt.

cards.question: God gives a picture for the neighbors who treat Israel with contempt. What are they like?

cards.text: God says Israel will no longer face a pricking brier or a painful thorn from all around them. That's the pebble finally coming out of your shoe after a whole day of walking on it.
Then the Lord GOD looks ahead. He will gather the house of Israel from the peoples they've been scattered among, and He will show Himself holy among them in the sight of the nations.

cards.question: Once God gathers the house of Israel, where does He say they will dwell?
God says He gave Israel's land to His servant ___.

cards.text: There they will dwell securely, build houses, and plant vineyards. After years in the back of a junk drawer, friend, a house with ROOM in it sounds like a dream to me.

cards.question: True or false: God says Israel will dwell securely when He judges those around them who treat them with contempt.

cards.text: And God closes with that line one more time: “Then they will know that I am the LORD their God.” This time, friend, it ends with two extra words: THEIR God.
